newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar stays firm as May expiry nears.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar stays firm as May expiry nears.

text.p: Cross and switch trades dominated white sugar futures on Tuesday as the market prepared for the expiry of the spot May contract, traders said.
Price movements were tight across the board and most of the day's heavy volume came from the nearby May/August crosses coupled with a sprinkling of against actuals trades.
October/May also featured as a cross.
Traders said the May expiry on April 15 was attracting more interest in the nearby spread as spot positions were rolled forward.

"It's people getting out of the May that is causing the volume in the whites," said one, adding that New York would have to break its own eight-week range for the London market to show much of an inclination to move.
At 1535 GMT May was up 60 cents at $310.60 and August up 10 cents at $307.90, leaving the spread towards the upper end of the day's trading range.
Market volume amounted to a hefty 3,160 lots.
White premiums against the New York narrowed slightly but little trading interest was reported.
"They've all come in a dollar over the past two or three days," the trader said. The May/May arbitrage is valued at around $67.
Market sources said the May whites expiry was likely to see a physical delivery of between two and three cargoes of European Union sugar.
The May contract in Paris also accounted for the bulk of the traded volume on the Matif market, which totalled 1,597 lots.
May was up 60 cents at $310.50 and August up 10 cents at $307.90.
